result:
Report written. Nine FEBio runs are healthy and the account's 32-core CPU limit is the bottleneck. I made one fix: re-pinned a slow run onto a single NUMA node.

**Running work:**
- A new batch started 03:55–03:59: 10 runs (physF4 and physF4dt).
- physF4_p139 finished normally at 04:28 after 1807 s.
- The other 9 are running: 7 on GPUs 1–4 and 2 on CPU only (physF4dt_p083 and physF4dt_p139).
- All 9 logs grew within the last 10 s, and every run has a checkpoint (`case.dmp`).

**Resources:**
- **CPU (the bottleneck):** 29.3 of 32 quota cores in use, and 16% of time slices are throttled. About 36 threads want to run, so each worker thread gets about 58%.
- **GPU:** utilisation is only 0–23% because the runs are held back on the CPU side.
- **Memory:** 134.3 of 137.4 GB, but only 32.7 GB is program memory; the rest is reclaimable page cache. No out-of-memory kills.
- **Disk:** /raid has 2.6 TB free.

**Queues:** the FEBio queue has 0 waiting, 9 running, 2559 done and 2 failed. The task queue has 0 waiting, 1 done and 5 failed (the old gate2 failures from 10-28).

**Services:** all tmux services are up. The one-shot jobs in `ops/resume_all.sh` all have their `.done` markers, and the watchdog covers the scheduler, GPU sampler and preflight.

**Action:** physF4dt_p139 had a CPU mask spread over 4 NUMA nodes (72, 84, 107, 110), and 2 of its threads kept landing on CPU 107. I re-pinned it with `taskset -a` to CPUs 107–110, which are on the node holding its memory. I did this for both the FEBio process (1709022) and its parent (1709019). Its CPU use went from about 232% (average) to 400% (a few seconds after the change). I changed no scheduler settings: the queue is empty, so there was nothing to reorder.

**Needs a person:**
- Once these 9 runs finish, both queues are empty and the account goes idle again. The next batch has to be decided and queued.
- The scheduler still hands out CPU masks that span NUMA nodes (physF4dt_p061, p062, p083). p061 had two threads on one CPU in 1 of 3 checks, so I didn't re-pin it. The real fix is for `h06`/`h18` in the old repo to give each run cores on one node; that code is outside my scope, so it's listed under requests.
- The QA failure (R10, D-20261103-9) is still open; it's a science issue, not operations.

Files are in `work/agents/foreman/`:
- report_20261105_0427.md
- status.json

I also added one line to `work/ops/foreman_actions.log`.
